newsitem.title: USA: CSX to put surcharge on some DAP rail shipments.
newsitem.headline: CSX to put surcharge on some DAP rail shipments.

text.p: CSX Corp will charge customers shipping diammonium phosphate from parts of Florida, North Carolina and Mississippi an additional $200.00 per railcar January 1 through March 31, said Karen Burns, a spokeswoman for CSX.
This is the first time CSX has imposed a DAP surcharge and it will apply to single car shipments on CSX equipment only, Burns said.
The surcharge is being imposed in an attempt to alleviate any railcar supply tightness during what is typically the busiest time for shipping fertilizer and grain, Burns said.
"It's an equipment utilization issue," Burns said. "The car type used for DAP and grain are the same, and that's a peak period for both of those commodities."
Analysts said the surcharge was high enough that it would be felt by DAP shippers.
"If it (the surcharge) were $50.00 a car, you probably wouldn't feel that," one commission house analyst said. "But $200.00, you're going to feel that."
Some fertilizer analysts were also looking for a jump in DAP shipments from the Southeast before the surcharge goes into effect.
